## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There is no evidence in this search yet. In generation 0, all 84 trials scored exactly 0, including training success, so we can't rank ideas or measure seed noise. The agent never learns to place bricks exactly right, even on the training stream. Architecture families from deep CNNs to transformers to layout-free heads all failed. That suggests the bottleneck is learning dynamics at this tiny budget (the default recipe allows only about 32 updates), not what the network can represent. The starting net can in principle express the rule 'land at the highest filled cell under the footprint, with every landing cell missing'. So round 1 probes settings that were never tried: lr above 2e-3, n_envs above 256, gae_lambda below 0.9, a much smaller network, and standard PPO orthogonal initialisation with near-uniform starting logits. Each probe is built to make reaching any nonzero training signal more likely, not to refine anything.

### Round 2
87 trials have now been run across both generations. Every one scored 0 on dev and 0 in training, so seed noise still can't be measured and no idea ranks above another. The three changes in round 1 also scored 0: a short-horizon recipe with high lr and big batches, a tiny network trained 1 epoch on about 426k steps, and standard PPO orthogonal initialisation. So the cause is probably not the learning rate, batch noise, initialisation or capacity. Two things the evidence doesn't rule out are long credit assignment for the +1 exact-build bonus and the DONE decision. To succeed, the agent must pick DONE at exactly the step the build becomes exact, which needs a sharp global "nothing missing" signal and a long horizon. Neither has been tested: gamma above 0.99 and gae_lambda above 0.95 were never tried. With no gradient to follow, I'm spending this round on three different untested directions.

### Round 3
Every trial scores 0.000, both on training and on dev, so seed noise still cannot be measured. A failure this uniform across many networks and recipes points to something systematic rather than slow learning. If per-placement accuracy were even moderate, some 6-brick targets would succeed by chance. One plausible block is DONE. Early in an episode DONE is always worse than a correct placement, so its logit is pushed down whenever there are missing cells. The state 'nothing missing' is almost never reached during exploration, so DONE is never learned and the agent keeps adding extra cells. Untested fix: give DONE and the value function a learned log-count of missing cells. A learned 1x1 conv reads the missing channels (selected, no bias), the outputs are made non-negative and summed over cells, then a log is taken. The count is exactly zero only when the build is complete, so the log becomes a clear outlier there. A negative weight learned from incomplete states then extrapolates to a high DONE logit at completion. All three candidates test this idea under different sample budgets and network sizes.

### Round 4
Every trial scored 0, both here and in generation 0 (93 trials). Training success was also 0, so nothing has been learned. None of these changed that: recipe settings (very low or very high gamma and lambda, lr 3e-3, 1024 envs, 1 to 8 epochs), init schemes, DONE detectors, normalisation with FiLM, or tiny and large nets. With no nonzero result, seed noise can't be measured and no idea can be ranked. Either exact builds are out of reach within this budget, or this world differs in a way none of the priors capture. This is the last round, so I spread three cheap, low-risk bets over ideas that haven't been tested: (1) many small, fully on-policy updates (64 envs, 1 epoch, ent 0, clip 0.3); (2) per-type learned convolutions shaped to each footprint with a one-cell rim, which see raw per-layer cells directly; (3) entropy 0.05 (above the 0.04 tried) with a long horizon.
